$comment: Risk class of every manifest v2 scope (plans/cmux-next/app-platform.md 12.5). One table for the validator, the supervisor's consent sheet and the store. Rules apply in order; the first match wins. cmux_app_manifest::capabilities checks it against generated/scopes.json: every op scope is decided by one rule (a scope that two patterns match gets a literal rule first), and a rule no op scope uses says in gates what it gates instead (extensibility-DESIGN.md 13).

classes.standard: Granted with the app; listed in Settings and revocable.
classes.sensitive: Shown highlighted on the consent sheet; revocable.
classes.restricted: First-party apps, or Verified apps whose review covers this scope. Unverified apps never hold it.
classes.elevated: Never granted at install. Any tier gets it only by an explicit user grant in the native confirmation sheet, with a warning (origin user).

rules.gates: a native app server's spawn of one bundled binary (server.scopes)
an app server's call of one named host op (server.scopes)
implementing cmux.terminal.backend/1 or cmux.terminal.connector/1 (interface ops, not catalog ops)

rules.$comment: the user's folders (plans/cmux-next/projects.md): paths stay on the Mac; no app reads or edits them without an explicit grant
the user's palette usage history (palette-ranking.md 5.3): local to the Mac, read and written by the app's palette only
the user's stashed web pages (stash-v1): what they read, and a restore opens URLs; first-party apps only
the user's sidebar document (sidebar-doc-v1): apps read it with the app, change it only by an explicit user grant, like sidebar_layout:write
the user's own sidebar arrangement (sidebar-sections.md 5): apps read it with the app, change it only by an explicit user grant

rules.gates: answers in a family other than feed (manifest scopes the schema allows; no catalog op needs one yet)
input to a family other than terminal (manifest scopes the schema allows; no catalog op needs one yet)

rules.$comment: create and revoke credentials of the family, for example coderouter:keys
rules.gates: provider ops the Mac app answers (coderouter:keys); they are not in scopes.json yet

rules.$comment: listing the team's connections and policy (integration.list); without this rule the generic :read rule and the provider rule integration:<provider> both match, and only their order made it standard. A provider cannot be named read.
